question: Do the 2022 Bicol River and Calabanga river studies support release-ready, site-specific fish occurrence rows for Bicol freshwater and estuarine habitats?

sourcesReviewed.citation: Bigueja, M. C., Bigueja, C. C., & Plantado, L. C. (2022). Diversity and Abundance of Fishes and Mollusks in Bicol River. THE American Journal of Humanities and Social Sciences Research, 5(4), 40-54.
sourcesReviewed.access: Full 15-page publisher-hosted PDF and journal homepage reviewed. The paper describes survey/test-fishing across upstream, midstream and downstream parts of the Bicol River in Camarines Sur. It lists upstream Baao, Nabua and Bula; midstream Naga, Minalabac, Milaor and Camaligan; downstream Gainza, Canaman, Pamplona, Magarao and Bombon.

reportedScope.waterbody: Bicol River, Camarines Sur study reach; not the entire river basin or every province crossed by the river.
reportedScope.surveySummary: The abstract reports 22 fish species (12 native, 10 introduced), including eight described as marine and one as invasive. It separately says 1,155 specimens belonged to 27 species and 22 families; the paper does not reconcile the differing scopes or the combined fish/macroinvertebrate totals.
reportedScope.dateAndStationPrecision: No field dates, station coordinates, vouchers or taxon-by-station crosswalk were located. Municipalities are associated with river sections, not individual capture records.
reportedScope.taxonomyAndHabitat: Table 1 mixes fish and macroinvertebrate entries and freshwater, marine and brackish-associated taxa. Source origin/invasive labels and taxonomic strings remain attributed source claims, not independently verified classifications.

qualityConcerns: Methods say 'three municipalities' upstream but enumerate three upstream, four midstream and five downstream localities; Gainza is duplicated in one study-area sentence.
The abstract reports 22 fish species but also 1,155 specimens across 27 species and 22 families without reconciling the totals.
The relative-abundance formula and prose give inconsistent denominators, including individuals versus total species.
There are no exact collection dates, named sampling stations or specimen/voucher crosswalks for taxon-by-site assertions.
Some classifications and scientific-name spellings require independent authority review.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: The PDF labels the paper Open Access and the journal calls itself open access, but no item-specific reuse license was found. Public access is not treated as permission to republish tables or use extracted rows. No table or figure was copied; publication approval is false.

sourcesReviewed.citation: Siares, I. F. N., & Bradecina, S. R. B. (2022). Diversity and Distribution of Ichthyofauna and Macro-invertebrates in Inarihan River, Calabanga, Camarines Sur. AGRIKULTURA: CBSUA Research and Innovation Journal, 3(1).
sourcesReviewed.access: Full 15-page publisher-hosted paper, article page and CBSUA journal copyright/license policy reviewed. The abstract describes Tigman, Hinagyanan and Inarihan rivers in Calabanga; detailed methods/results and title emphasize Inarihan. Dry/wet season sampling is reported, but not calendar months or dates.

reportedScope.methods: The paper describes seine or hand-net fish collection and stream reaches/replicates; it says GPS centroids were taken, but a station-coordinate to fish-taxon crosswalk is not published in the reviewed article.
reportedScope.taxonSummary: The abstract reports total on-site taxa per river across organism groups. These 32/25/21 values must not be represented as fish-only richness; the paper separately reports fish genera and macroinvertebrates.
reportedScope.dateAndStationPrecision: Only wet/dry season labels are supplied, not exact dates. Methods name Siba-o, Fabrica and Sugod as Inarihan sampling locations, but the broader three-river claim is not fully reconciled with the Inarihan-focused fish tables and locations.

qualityConcerns: The three-river abstract and Inarihan-focused methods do not provide a complete river/station/taxon register.
Dry- and wet-season fish totals and printed table rows show count, duplicate and spelling inconsistencies.
The relative-abundance denominator is described inconsistently.
Some downstream taxa are described as brackish-associated; the section label 'freshwater fishes' alone does not classify every record as freshwater.
No month/day field dates, voucher identifiers or complete station/taxon crosswalk were identified.
sourcesReviewed.reuse: CBSUA's journal copyright/license policy states articles remain open access under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International and permits attributed quotation; full-article republication requires written publisher permission. This review stores metadata and a brief assessment only, copies no table/figure and grants no app-publication approval.

crossSourceAssessment.overlap: Both studies add historical Camarines Sur river leads but share no station IDs, specimen accessions or collection-date crosswalk. Citation of the earlier multi-habitat survey is not independent replication.
crossSourceAssessment.freshwaterAndEstuarySeparation: The Bicol River study reach includes downstream influence toward San Miguel Bay and the Calabanga paper explicitly includes an estuary. Keep freshwater reaches, brackish/downstream habitat and marine-affinity taxa distinct.
crossSourceAssessment.appReadiness: Research leads only. Neither paper establishes current presence, complete basin coverage, precise occurrence geometry, present abundance, diet, catchability, fishing access, legality or safety.
crossSourceAssessment.coverageMeaning: The studies broaden Bicol river/estuary literature coverage but do not complete Camarines Sur, Bicol Region, Luzon or the Philippines.

rightsReview.bicolRiverPaper: No item-specific reuse license verified despite the Open Access label. Do not reproduce tables, figures or derived app rows without clear terms or permission.
rightsReview.calabangaRiversPaper: CBSUA journal policy specifies CC BY 4.0. Attribute authors, journal, publisher and license if later used; full article republication requires written permission.

disposition.reason: Exact dates and taxon/station crosswalks are missing; habitat scope mixes freshwater and estuary; totals/method descriptions are inconsistent; and the Bicol River article lacks item-specific reuse terms. The CBSUA paper's stated CC BY 4.0 policy does not resolve its site/taxon inconsistencies.

nextAction: Screen the 2021 Bicol River target/non-target catch-shift study for exact dates and locations, and determine whether its evidence represents fisher landings rather than direct river occurrences. Continue separate lake and tributary research across Lake Bato, Lake Baao-Bula, Pawili/Agos and other Bicol inland waters.

sources.supports: Full 2022 Bicol River article, reported reach/locality scope, mixed fish/invertebrate content, abstract count conflicts, methods limitations and lack of dates/voucher crosswalk.
Journal homepage identifies THE AJHSSR as open access; no item-specific license was established for the article.
Official CBSUA article record, authors, abstract and three-river Calabanga scope.
Full 2022 article methods, seasonal labels, collection approach, river/site scope, taxon-table limitations and absence of exact field dates.
CBSUA journal copyright/license policy states CC BY 4.0 and describes attribution/full-article reproduction terms.
